answer: The protocol enforces sybil resistance by requiring agents to maintain 1,000 unique data shards, verified through unpredictable retrieval audits where any failed proof of replication triggers a non-refundable slash of deposited funds. An honest agent incurs a baseline storage cost, while 1,000 fakes must pay 1,000 times that expense. Like a lonely island of bits, each shard rests within a secure vault, acting as a unique digital fable of provenance that no colluding party can replicate or forge. The audit remains binding for 30 days, ensuring integrity across the network.
